note: Per-material transparency of strategic reserves. The honest axis is not "who holds a buffer" (the US NDS and China SRB both hold materials) but "whose buffer is quantified in the open" — only Japan (JOGMEC) publishes per-material days of cover. Curated + web-verified.

regimes.fact: DLA Strategic Materials holds ~28 commodities (incl. cobalt, tungsten, tantalum, titanium sponge, beryllium, germanium); the inventory is ~$1.0-1.4bn vs a ~$14.8-15.5bn identified shortfall — small in dollar terms, and per-material days of cover are not published.
regimes.verdict: Holds materials, but small relative to identified need and not published on a days-of-cover basis.

regimes.fact: Stockpiles 7 rare metals (incl. cobalt, tungsten, manganese, vanadium, nickel) at ~60 days of consumption; target up to 180 days for high-risk.
regimes.verdict: The model — the only country publishing per-material days of cover.

regimes.fact: Holds a rare-metals reserve and publishes coverage TARGETS (e.g. days-of-cover goals), though per-material current levels are less granular than JOGMEC.
regimes.verdict: A second allied programme with public targets — so "only Japan" is about published per-material cover specifically.

regimes.fact: Holds rare earths, cobalt and others — levels undisclosed.
regimes.verdict: Real but opaque: an information asymmetry as much as a material one.

regimes.fact: A strategic reserve is proposed under the Critical Raw Materials Act.
